contentfulBlogPost.title: Digital Online Store: End-to-End E-Commerce Platform

childMarkdownRemark.html:
Project overview

  • Role: Co-owner, UI/UX Designer & Front-end Developer
  • Timeline: May 2020 – December 2020
  • Sector: E-Commerce / Creative Retail
  • Platform: WordPress, WooCommerce, Adobe XD, HTML5/CSS3
  • Core skills demonstrated: End-to-end product design, wireframing, e-commerce conversion rate optimisation (CRO), design systems, WooCommerce theme customisation, digital fulfilment workflows.

What this project proves about me: I can bridge commercial strategy, user experience architecture, and hands-on front-end development to launch a viable, automated e-commerce venture from scratch.

Desktop viewport mock-up showcasing the final high-contrast branding, promotional value proposition, and structured catalogue layout for the digital artwork storefront.

The challenge

Independent creative businesses frequently face a friction trap: third-party marketplaces charge substantial transaction fees and dilute brand equity, while bespoke e-commerce builds often introduce excessive administrative complexity for non-technical store managers.

As co-owner, my objective was twofold:

  1. User Experience & CRO: Provide prospective art buyers with a fast, credible, and frictionless browsing-to-download path, avoiding the drop-offs typical of digital download delivery.
  2. Store Administration: Build an intuitive content management architecture enabling non-technical stakeholders to upload new digital assets, manage promotional pricing, and monitor orders without touching code.

Constraints included a lean operational budget, zero dedicated server administration resource, and the requirement for automated digital asset delivery immediately post-transaction.

My process

  1. Market Discovery & Requirements Gathering: Analysed competitor digital download experiences, establishing baseline user expectations for file delivery, previews, and licensing clarity.
  2. Information Architecture & Wireframing: Outlined the primary purchase flow (discovery → product view → checkout → download retrieval) using low-fidelity prototypes in Adobe XD.
  3. Modular Header & Visual Exploration: Tested twelve distinct header and hero banner arrangements to balance promotional impact against catalog visibility.
  4. High-Fidelity Prototyping & Design Systems: Layered an accessible, vibrant colour palette (black, white, vibrant yellow, and cyan) with strong typographic hierarchy to build trust and energy.
  5. CMS Implementation & Custom Development: Configured WooCommerce on WordPress, streamlining checkout fields and automating secure digital product delivery.

What I did

Information architecture and low-fidelity prototypes

To ensure the path to purchase remained clear, I started in Adobe XD by mapping out the core user flows. Digital goods demand higher initial trust than physical goods—users need immediate clarity on what file formats they will receive, file resolutions, and how delivery functions.

I structured early wireframes to prioritise product imagery, clear technical specifications (aspect ratio, dpi, licensing rights), and a distraction-free single-page checkout flow.

Low-fidelity wireframe series outlining the structural hierarchy across catalogue discovery, product specification details, checkout input fields, and the transaction confirmation screen.

I subsequently validated the layout mechanics through iterative structural layouts, ensuring the relationship between product cards, promotional sidebars, and order confirmation states maintained logical continuity across varying screen widths.

Sequential low-fidelity user flow evaluating catalogue grid density, secondary product details, and the post-purchase receipt page highlighting download link placement.

Homepage header explorations

The hero header was the primary lever to drive initial engagement and communicate store value. Because the store owner needed the ability to run frequent seasonal promotions without breaking page layouts, I created a componentised hero system.

I evaluated twelve distinct structural configurations in Adobe XD, testing split-screen layouts, typography alignments, CTA placements, and colour distribution between primary yellow accents and secondary dark backgrounds.

Exploratory matrix of twelve homepage header compositions testing visual weight, typography balance, call-to-action prominence, and background colour distribution.

High-fidelity prototypes and final product enhancements

Transitioning from structural layouts to high fidelity, I balanced a high-energy aesthetic with functional minimalism. The primary palette combined high-contrast black and white for readability, paired with warm yellow (#FFD000 range) and turquoise/cyan accents to evoke modern creativity.

I iterated multiple homepage variants to determine how promotional units interacted with top-selling product categories, ensuring commercial drivers did not overpower organic browsing.

Three high-fidelity homepage layout variations exploring the integration of hero banners, curated collections, and best-seller product grids using the final colour system.

Why I made these decisions

  • WordPress + WooCommerce as the platform foundation: Rather than building a headless custom application or relying on restrictive hosted SaaS platforms, WordPress provided open-source ownership, low operating overhead, and an intuitive UI for non-technical co-owners to manage inventory and view sales analytics.
  • Optimised digital-only checkout pipeline: Physical shipping address fields, courier selectors, and unnecessary form elements were stripped out entirely. Standard checkout fields were reduced by more than 50%, removing unnecessary user input friction and minimising drop-off.
  • Automated asynchronous asset delivery: To eliminate customer support enquiries regarding download links, file delivery was automated across two channels simultaneously: an encrypted, instant download link on the order confirmation screen and a transactional receipt email containing redundant links and format instructions.
  • Modular, component-based header: Designing a flexible hero component allowed store managers to switch promotional messaging and background schemes directly from the CMS without requiring template re-coding.

Impact / results

Focus Area Solution Implemented Operational / UX Result
Checkout Flow Stripped physical shipping fields for digital items Frictionless 1-page checkout flow requiring minimal fields
Fulfilment Encrypted instant file delivery pipeline 100% automated asset delivery; zero manual file handling required
Content Management Custom WooCommerce fields and intuitive UI Complete non-technical catalog management independence
Brand Architecture Modular header and responsive colour system Consistent cross-device presentation validated across viewports

Tools and skills applied

Category Tools / Skills
UX & Product Design Information architecture, user journey mapping, low-to-high fidelity wireframing, Adobe XD
UI & Visual Design Design systems, typographic hierarchy, responsive layout, promotional visual exploration
Front-End & CMS WordPress, WooCommerce, HTML5, CSS3, PHP template customisation
Operations & CRO Digital asset security, checkout funnel optimisation, product catalogue structuring

Roles performed on this project

  • Product Owner & Co-owner: Formulated commercial model, defined product scope, and prioritised feature releases.
  • Lead UI/UX Designer: Led user journey design, wireframing, component exploration, and high-fidelity interactive prototyping.
  • Front-end Developer: Configured WordPress and WooCommerce, applied custom styling, and automated transactional workflows.

childMarkdownRemark.excerpt: Designed and developed an end-to-end WordPress e-commerce store for custom digital downloads, combining modular layout systems with…

childMarkdownRemark.html: Operating as co-owner, designer, and developer, I established a dedicated e-commerce storefront for selling custom digital download art prints. The central challenge was bridging two distinct operational needs: providing an engaging, conversion-optimised checkout journey for non-technical shoppers, while establishing a decoupled, easily manageable content management system (CMS) that required zero technical overhead for daily inventory updates. Using an iterative process in Adobe XD, I mapped customer journeys, developed wireframes, and tested twelve homepage header configurations to establish strong brand distinction. I then implemented the full platform on WordPress and WooCommerce, building custom templates and digital fulfilment workflows. The final product delivered a responsive, high-performance storefront with automated instant-download delivery, eliminating post-purchase support friction and empowering autonomous inventory management.
